description: Pairwise distance matrix of a multiple alignment as EMBOSS 6.6.0 distmat (every correction and option, verified on 1 100 + 600 runs of the installed program, single-precision arithmetic as in distmat.c): matches = columns where both rows carry the same non-gap symbol, g = columns where either row has a gap; 'uncorrected' D = 1 - matches/(L - g + g*gapWeight); 'jukes-cantor' -b*ln(1 - D/b) with b = 3/4 (nucleotide) or 19/20 (protein); 'kimura' = Kimura 2-parameter (nucleotides) / Kimura protein -ln(1 - D - 0.2 D^2) (proteins); 'tamura', 'tajima-nei' and 'jin-nei' (Gamma distance; calculateA / parameterA) are nucleotide methods. ambiguous counts ambiguity codes (proteins: B/Z/J/X weights; nucleotides: distmat's ajBaseAlphacharCompare with its own defects, and a gap in the first sequence of a pair makes the program loop forever = tool error). position = 123 (all codon bases, default), 12, or 1 / 2 / 3 (nucleotides); tajima-nei and protein kimura with a position other than 123 read beyond the program's buffers (undefined) = tool error. Fractions, not percent; entries with a zero denominator or a saturated logarithm are null. Rows are read as EMBOSS reads an alignment (A4-3): letters and '*' are kept, '.' '~' '-' are gaps, '?' '#' '+' are the unknown residue, every other character (digits, blanks, '_', punctuation) is dropped.

sequences.description: At least two aligned sequences of equal length.

residueType.description: 'auto' (default; EMBOSS decides from the first row), 'nucleotide' or 'protein'.

calculateA.description: distmat -calculatea: calculate the Jin-Nei parameter a instead of using parameterA (default false).

parameterA.description: distmat -parametera: the Jin-Nei Gamma parameter a (default 1.0).

sequenceQualifiers.description: EMBOSS sequence-input qualifiers as on the command line: -sbegin 3 -send -2 -sreverse -slower -supper -scircular -snucleotide -sprotein (begin / end 1-based, negative = from the end; -sreverse reverse-complements a nucleotide sequence, the range then refers to the original). Measured on EMBOSS 6.6.0 per program: distmat ignores -sbegin / -send; -sreverse reverse-complements every row of a nucleotide set; the set is nucleotide when its first row is (or -snucleotide); a protein set uses proteinMethod. The text is resolved exactly as the EMBOSS program resolves it on its command line after the sequence arguments (ACD, 6.6.0): -sbegin1 3, -sbegin1=3, -nosreverse1, -sreverse1 N, any case, -/--/ prefix, and every UNIQUE abbreviation (-sbeg1, -sre2; uniqueness is decided among all qualifiers of the program, an ambiguous or unknown one is refused). The number is the sequence (1, and 2 for the second sequence of a two-sequence program; 1 for a program with one sequence). An unnumbered qualifier belongs to the LAST sequence given (-sbegin 3 is -sbegin2 3 in a two-sequence program) until a qualifier of another sequence ends that tie; after that it applies to all sequences. -sformat selects the file format of the text; -ufo -fformat -fopenfile name the feature file of a program that takes the features of its sequences (diffseq: the files are given by the tool); -sask -squick -sdbname -sid -iquery are accepted without effect (residue strings have no file); any other qualifier or a stray word is refused.

proteinMethod.description: distmat -protmethod for a protein set when sequenceQualifiers is given: same names as method (default: the same as method).

matrix.description: Symmetric distance matrix (fractions, zero diagonal; null = undefined or saturated).

errors.message: At least two sequences are required
